newsitem.title: FRANCE: Virgin launches cola in France with spoof ads.
newsitem.headline: Virgin launches cola in France with spoof ads.

text.p: Britain's Virgin Group, aiming to snatch the number two slot from Pepsico's Pepsi Cola in France, is running a series of spoof adverts this month to coincide with the launch of Virgin Cola on the French market.

The campaign, which parodies conventional soft-drink ads, began on Saturday for the cola, which Virgin is selling at a five to 10 percent discount to market leader Coca Cola's Coke, Olivier Lefaivre, communications manager at Virgin Cola France, said on Monday.

Low pricing and irreverent publicity has become the hallmark of the company created by British entrepreneur Richard Branson, which has in recent years created brands ranging from financial services to vodka under the Virgin name.
Virgin Cola was first test marketed in Britain from 1994 in Tesco supermarkets, but has only been more widely available there since May this year.

In France, the only other European market targeted by Virgin Cola, the drink has been tested for a year in Monoprix stores and has been sold in four other supermarket and hypermarket chains since June, Lefaivre said.
Although Branson is not as well known in France as he is in Britain, the Virgin name gets surprisingly high recognition scores here.

A survey by market research institute Ifop for Virgin last year found 80 percent of the 15-35 age-group recognised the name, mainly because of the five Virgin Megastore giant record shops in France and the Virgin record label, Lefaivre said.
"We are above all playing on the image of Virgin. Everyone knows Virgin through the Megastores," he said.

"Faced with a market plunged into a sort of lethargy, where competitors are rare, Virgin Cola is offering a real alternative... with a young, fun and cool image," Virgin Cola France said in a statement on the product launch.
The advertising campaign aims to caricature the ad scenarios used by the big American firms and use crazy humour, Virgin Cola France said in a statement.

Devised by agency Rainey Kelly Campbell Roalfe, which handles Virgin Group's advertising, the campaign will run for three weeks on terrestrial channel M6, pay TV channel Canal Plus and on cable channels such as Serie Club and Fun TV with young audiences.

One of the three spots shows an aerobics class of rounded Brazilian youngsters dressed in vibrant, acid-coloured gym-wear sipping the "light" version of Virgin Cola. Another features an Italian nun giving in to the temptation of a Virgin Cola.
French consumers tend to be hooked on mineral water, a characteristic which has made launching new soft drink brands hard in France.

The cola segment is dominated, as elsewhere, by Coca Cola with a share of some 80 percent, while Pepsi, which has been losing market share, takes 10 to 12 percent of the market, according to recent studies.
"Virgin Cola aims to become the second brand in the cola segment very quickly," a statement from Virgin Cola France said.
Virgin Cola has also been test marketed in Australia, Japan and in the United States, where it is due to be launched more widely soon, Lefaivre said.
